prompt_text: Who is the best HVAC company in Atlanta to replace my air conditioner?
answer_verbatim:
Short answer: there’s no single “best” HVAC company for everyone — the best choice depends on your location in the Atlanta metro area, budget, the size/age of your home, the system you want, and whether you value lowest price, longest warranty, or best workmanship. I can help you pick the top options near you if you give your ZIP code and any brand or budget preferences.

If you want to evaluate companies yourself, here’s a quick roadmap and shortlist of what to look for.

How to choose the best company
- Get at least 3 written estimates (same scope) that include equipment model, SEER rating, exact tonnage, labor, ductwork changes, permits, and disposal.  
- Make sure they do a Manual J load calculation (right size unit) and will inspect/quote any needed ductwork.  
- Check credentials: NATE-certified technicians, ACCA membership or contractor association, valid business license and general liability insurance. Ask for license/insurance numbers and verify.  
- Read recent reviews on Google, Yelp, BBB and look for responses from the company. Prioritize installers with many local, recent 4–5 star reviews.  
- Ask about warranties: manufacturer parts warranty and labor/installation warranty (5–10 years is common for labor from reputable dealers). Ask who honors the warranty (the company or the manufacturer dealer network).  
- Confirm rebates/financing: ask about utility rebates (Georgia Power, municipal programs), tax credits, and 0%/low-interest financing offers.  
- Beware very low bids — they often mean undersized equipment, short warranties, or add-ons later.

What to ask during estimates
- Will you perform a Manual J/M and provide a written report?  
- Exact model and SEER, condenser and air handler/evaporator coil part numbers.  
- Total installed price and itemized list (equipment, labor, permits, ductwork, disposal).  
- Estimated install timeline, start date, and how many technicians.  
- Warranty details (parts and labor) and post-install service policy.  
- Are technicians NATE-certified? Will permits be pulled? Who inspects final work?

Typical cost ranges (Atlanta area, ballpark)
- Replacement only (like-for-like, average home): roughly $4,000–$8,000 for a standard 2–3.5 ton system.  
- Upgrades to higher-efficiency systems, new ductwork, or larger homes: $8,000–$15,000+.  
(Prices vary widely by house size, SEER, brand, and ductwork.)

Brands & financing
- Common quality brands: Trane, Carrier, Lennox, Goodman, Rheem, York. Pick a reputable local dealer for the brand you prefer.  
- Ask about manufacturer rebates/extended warranties for dealer-installed systems and financing plans.

Where to search for contractors
- Google Maps / Yelp (sort by rating and recent reviews)  
- Better Business Bureau (BBB) ratings and complaint history  
- Nextdoor or local Facebook groups for neighborhood referrals  
- HomeAdvisor / Angi for matched pros (but verify independent reviews)

If you want, I can:
- Pull top-rated HVAC installers near your ZIP code and summarize ratings, specialties, and typical warranties; or  
- Give a checklist you can hand to techs during estimates.

Which would you prefer? If you share your Atlanta ZIP code and any preferences (brand, budget, timeline), I’ll find 3–5 well-reviewed local installers and summarize pros/cons for each.
